partial_progress.details: Phases 1-3 of 4 completed and committed. Phase 4 (redeploy + full gate set) is blocked: sibling task 371 has live, uncommitted edits to agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/roadmap-integration.sh and scripts/tests/test-roadmap-generation.sh, confirmed via git log to be 371's own in-progress work on top of its committed history. deploy-headless.sh regenerates the whole deployed tree unconditionally from current filesystem state, so running it now would capture 371's in-progress, unverified edit outside this task's control. memory_candidates.content: When a plan phase's verification tier uses doc-lint (check-extension-docs.sh / verify-deploy.sh --only-gate 3,4) and the phase edits a markdown file under agent-system/extensions/*/context/**, expect index-entries.json's line_count field for that file's entry to go stale immediately -- doc-lint's Rule R checks it against the actual file. The sanctioned one-shot remedy is `bash .claude/scripts/generate-context-line-counts.sh --write` run from the DEPLOYED scripts/ tree (it refuses to run from the agent-system source-store copy, with a clear error naming why), which corrects only the entries that are actually stale and leaves the rest untouched -- safe to run even when a concurrent sibling task has already correctly updated other entries in the same shared index-entries.json. Since that file is often itself a declared concurrent sibling's file_scope, commit the correction as a small separate follow-up via git-commit-scoped.sh rather than folding it into the phase's own git-commit-phase.sh call, to avoid the Phase-Commit Containment Self-Check dropping it as out-of-this-task's-declared-scope.

deploy-headless.sh regenerates the WHOLE deployed .claude/ tree from current filesystem state, with no per-task or per-file scoping flag. On a shared working tree with a concurrently-dispatched sibling task, check git status --porcelain for the sibling's own declared file_scope paths immediately before running it -- a live, uncommitted edit there means deploying now would capture the sibling's in-progress, unverified work. git log on those paths distinguishes 'sibling's own prior commits, now with a further uncommitted diff on top' (defer) from 'nothing recent, dirty for an unrelated reason' (investigate further). There is no sanctioned wait-for-sibling-to-finish mechanism (external-process-wait.md and bounded-build-waiter.md both cover a process this dispatch itself started, not another agent's work) -- the correct response is to stop, record the blocker via issue-record.sh, close the phase [PARTIAL] with a handoff naming the concrete resume condition, and return status partial rather than spin-polling or proceeding.
